newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Slow trade dampens Moroccan stocks.
newsitem.headline: Slow trade dampens Moroccan stocks.

text.p: The Casablanca stock exchange closed on Thursday 0.13 percent lower as blue chips stocks ONA, Banque Commerciale du Maroc and Wafabank dipped after recent gains, stockbrokers said.
The bourse all-share index closed at 647.27 points, down from 648.11 on Wednesday.
"The increases of these last days were the result of a brief demand but overall the market is slow," a broker at BMCI Securities said.
ONA, the biggest Moroccan private conglomerate, dropped six to 814 dirhams.
In the banking sector, BCM fell 13 dirhams to 890 dirhams and Wafabank was down 10 dirhams to 810 dirhams.
Credit firms Credor rose 11 dirhams to 756 dirhams and Maghrebail was unchanged at 518 dirhams. Best performer was Eqdom Credit which advanced 24 dirhams to 1,115 dirhams.
First tranche of privatisation bonds, issued in January 1996, gained three dirhams to 1,370 dirhams while the second issue from May 1996 edged down two dirhams to 1,204 dirhams.

The bonds had initially a nominal price of 1,000 dirhams. They give holders preferential options on shares and the right to convert them in privatised companies or to sell them back at 8.0 percent interest a year.
"There are rumours of two new flotations so that they can absorb first tranche of privatisation bonds. Then there might be an issue of a third tranche soon," the broker added.
SNI, Societe Nationale d'Investissement, the second largest private group, was up three dirhams to 745 dirhams.
In the energy sector, mining firm Societe Metallurgique d'Imiter dipped nine dirhams to 560 dirhams.
Total traded volume on the official market was 29.4 million from 37.7 million dirhams.
On the over-the-counter market, the volume was 11.4 million dirhams from 16.8 million dirhams. Main trade was in more than 5,300 shares followed by some 3,700 Wafabank, the broker said.
